blocks.content: Before starting this course you should have completed the React Hooks course, or at minimum be comfortable with:

items: useEffect() for fetching data and running side effects
useRef() for DOM references and values that don't trigger re-renders
useMemo() for memoizing expensive computed values
Custom hooks for extracting and reusing stateful logic

blocks.content: If any of those feel shaky, go back and review the corresponding lesson before continuing. This course builds directly on top of those concepts.
One optional but helpful thing to understand is how the browser loads JavaScript bundles.
Chapter 4 on React.lazy will be a lot clearer if you have a rough mental model of what a "bundle" is and why splitting it matters.
We'll explain it when we get there, but a bit of prior exposure helps.
Use this space for your doubts about this lesson. Ask us anything that's confusing and our experts will provide explanations to help you understand.
